notes.title: Titan Talk and Hotfix Roundup March 13th
notes.content:
Did you miss Titan Talk yesterday! No worries, here is a summary!



   
[b]Special Guest: Kellen[/b]
        [list]            [*]                
Audio Manager at Titan Forge, working on Smite for almost 11 years
            [/*]            [*]                
Oversees and directs audio/music for the game
            [/*]            [*]                
Collaborates with various departments to ensure seamless audio integration
                    [/*][/list]
Kellen joined the show to discuss the ongoing work on Smite’s music and audio systems, along with the team’s approach to bug fixes and upcoming improvements.
[h2]Housekeeping & Recent Bug Fixes[/h2][list]    [*]        
[b]Hot Fixes Deployed:[/b]
        [olist]            [*]                
Fixed an issue where minions dealt no damage to familiars or pets.
            [/*]            [*]                
Further potential fix for the mini map overlay bug appearing in the store.
            [/*]            [*]                
Resolved an issue with the Health Chalice not refilling on respawn if it had zero charges upon player death.
            [/*]            [*]                
Fixed an audio bug causing the “ally has left the game” sound to play in post-match lobbies.
            [/*]            [*]                
Restored music packs functionality in Assault mode.
            [/*]            [*]                
Updated Aladdin’s lamp inventory behavior to prevent despawning other active items.
            [/*]            [*]                
Fixed Zeus’s ultimate hit sound on his T5 (and base) skin so it now plays the correct effect.
            [/*]            [*]                
Modified Bari’s Sacred Bell projectile and warning circle visuals to be more clear.
            [/*]        [/olist]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Known Issues & Ongoing Work:[/b]
        [list]            [*]                
[b]Pele’s Pyroclast Return:[/b] Investigating a bug with Pele’s pyroclast projectiles not returning properly.
            [/*]            [*]                
[b]Silent Wish Chest Ghost Rolls:[/b] Working on a fix for ghost roll issues—players will not lose any currency in the meantime.
            [/*]            [*]                
Several other bug fixes mentioned by the dev team, including:
                [list]                    [*]                        
Ymir Wall & Yemoja 3 incorrectly breaking Magi’s.
                    [/*]                    [*]                        
Bari’s Mystic Surge incorrectly tracking minion/jungle camp kills.
                    [/*]                    [*]                        
Match audio persisting into the end-of-match lobby.
                    [/*]                [/list]            [/*]        [/list]    [/*][/list][h2]Music & Audio in Smite 2[/h2]
[h3]Music Packs Overview[/h3]
[b]New in Smite 2:[/b] Music packs have finally been introduced in Open Beta 5. These allow players to customize their in-game music, from the fountain-lobby intro track to epic kill streak pieces.
[list]    [*]        
[b]Why Music Packs?[/b]
        [list]            [*]                
Adds new layers of personalization and immersion.
            [/*]            [*]                
Dynamic music triggers for taking down objectives, kills, and more.
            [/*]            [*]                
A broad range of musical styles from calm lofi to heavy metal.
            [/*]        [/list]    [/*][/list][h3]Top 10 Most-Equipped Music Packs (from Smite 1)[/h3][olist]    [*]        
[b]Jetpack Fighter[/b] – Surprising #1 pick with an energetic, futuristic vibe.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Ruby (Licensed)[/b]
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Slushy (Licensed)[/b]
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Cyber Tokyo[/b] – Dark synthwave inspiration.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]From the Nether[/b] – Spooky, ominous undertones.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Spirit Guide[/b] – Epic orchestral adventure feel.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Senpai[/b] – Anime-inspired, lively track.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Hellfire Syndicate[/b] – Metal-meets-hip-hop for a demonic/fashion vibe.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Heavenly Hymns[/b] – Ethereal and classic Smite orchestral.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Pirate[/b] – An adventurous pirate-themed rock mix.
    [/*][/olist] 
Note: Some licensed packs cannot be carried forward into Smite 2.
[h3]Kellen’s Personal Favorites[/h3]
Kellen, who oversees much of the audio direction, listed his top picks:
[olist]    [*]        
[b]Worlds Collide[/b] – A unique fusion of lofi and metal elements.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Season of Souls[/b] – Dark and intense metal reminiscent of fast-paced action games.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Chibi Mech[/b] – High-energy and upbeat EDM/trance blend.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Sea Shanty[/b] – Features actual Hi-Rez employees singing a jaunty pirate tune.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Arcane Purity[/b] – Magical orchestral vibe ideal for a wizardly or mystical mood.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Divine Uprising[/b] – Classic, epic orchestral theme.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Bollywood[/b] – Vibrant, culturally-inspired track that’s a hidden gem.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Lo-Fi[/b] – Perfect for chill gaming sessions.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Prism of Soul[/b] – Epic, slightly tragic orchestral piece.
    [/*][/olist]
Each pack was created by partnering with a range of composers, followed by feedback and iteration rounds. Some highlight collaborations have been done with producers like Andrea Bellucci, as well as artists from the metal band Hath.
[h2]Behind the Scenes: Audio Direction[/h2][h3]How Audio Themes Are Crafted[/h3][list]    [*]        
[b]Collaboration with God Designers:[/b] Kellen meets with design teams to understand a character’s abilities, tone, and needs.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Sound Palettes:[/b] Each god or theme receives a “sound palette” to set cohesive elements and textures across all abilities.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Iterative Development:[/b] Feedback is crucial—multiple revisions happen before finalizing a set of sounds.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Challenges:[/b] Avoiding overly literal sounds (e.g., barking bunnies) and ensuring variety among thematically similar gods.
    [/*][/list][h3]Dynamic Mixing & Future Audio Improvements[/h3][list]    [*]        
[b]Dynamic Mixing:[/b] Adjusts volume and intensity of different sounds (e.g. hits, global events) in real-time.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Potential Upcoming Tech:[/b] Expanding dynamic mixing for better hit feedback, better positional audio, and more.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Music Packs[/b]: Kellen teases an idea to create a possible “music pack playlist” system, letting players select and randomize segments from their owned packs.
    [/*][/list][h3]Working on Licensed Music & Projects[/h3][list]    [*]        
[b]Slipknot Collaboration:[/b] A huge highlight, culminating in exclusive Slipknot crossover packs & skins. Kellen recounts meeting the band and how important authenticity is in such high-profile partnerships.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Monster Cat & Other Collaborations:[/b] Deeper behind-the-scenes look at how new partnerships evolve and factor into Smite’s audio identity.
    [/*][/list][h2]Community Q&A Highlights[/h2][list]    [*]        
[b]Announcer Packs:[/b] The team is looking into bringing them to Smite 2. This includes the beloved Cthulhu and Lorelady versions, plus potential new ones.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Zeus T5 Audio Issue:[/b] Recently addressed so T5 Zeus’s ultimate & hit sounds now match the intended design.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]DJ Skins Playing Music Together:[/b] Formerly a complicated system in Smite 1, but it may be easier in UE5. The team is investigating ways to bring back group-synced music.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Sun Wukong/Guan Yu Drums:[/b] Classic requests to restore old, iconic drum sounds and themes. It’s under consideration for the future.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Upcoming Gods & Audio Teaser:[/b] Next god’s name starts with an H — and yes, they have a voice.
    [/*][/list][h2]Key Dates & Events[/h2][list]    [*]        
[b]Pele Pyroclast Fix:[/b] Ongoing investigation to ensure return projectiles function properly.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Silent Wish Chest Issue:[/b] Being resolved so ghost rolls no longer occur.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Community Tournaments:[/b] Nika and Hazer are hosting the Smite 2 Euros. Catch the drafts and matches this week.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]St. Patrick’s Day Event (Starting Friday):[/b] Complete matches to unlock the Celtic Music Pack for free.
    [/*][/list][h2]Final Takeaways[/h2][list]    [*]        
[b]Continuous Updates:[/b] The Smite 2 team is rapidly tackling bugs, performance improvements, and community feedback.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Ever-Evolving Audio:[/b] Music packs add flavor; new dynamic mixing systems are on the horizon, with Kellen constantly refining the in-game soundscape.
    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Stay Connected:[/b] More shows coming, including Monday’s “Merlin” reveal episode. Don’t miss the daily news on bug fixes, new features, and Q&A!
    [/*][/list]

[h3]Here are the items that have been hotfixed in the last 24 hours:[/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where Bari could get an extra enhanced ability
[*] Fixed an issue with Pele’s Pyroclast where return charges were not properly registering

[/list]

notes.title: Titan Talks and Hotfix Round Up
notes.content:
A small hotfix has gone out to address a number of issues the team is working on. There are still some other high priority ones in process, but we did not want to hold these:

[list]    [*]Fixed an issue where minions were dealing no damage to familiars.[/*]    [*]Made another potential fix to Store Overlay issues reported on console[/*]    [*]Fixed an issue with Health Chalice where if it had 0 charges and a player dies, it won’t refill[/*]    [*]Fixed an audio issue at end of match (“Ally has left the game”)[/*]    [*]Fixed an issue where Music Packs weren’t working Assault[/*]    [*]Aladdin - Moving the Lamp in his inventory no longer despawns other active items[/*]    [*]Fixed a sound effects issue where Zeus was playing the wrong hit sound[/*]    [*]Made an effects change to Bari Sacred Bell projectile and animation of warning circles[/*][/list][h3]Also, Titan Talks covered a number of topics around the release of Open Beta 5 on Monday but in case you missed it here are the highlights:[/h3][list]    [*]        
[b]Princess Bari (New God)[/b]
        [list]            [*][b]First deity from the Korean Pantheon[/b].[/*]            [*]Relies on [b]bell combos[/b] and a unique [b]spirit bar[/b] instead of traditional mana.[/*]            [*]Dynamic, combo-oriented kit, with powerful synergy around her abilities.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]New & Returning Skins[/b]
        [list]            [*][b]Silent Wish Aladdin[/b]: Exclusive to SMITE 2, available in the Silent Strike chest.[/*]            [*][b]Classic Skins [/b]now live:[list]                    [*]Steel Samurai Susano[/*]                    [*]Pool Party Jing Wei[/*]                [/list]            [/*]            [*][b]Cross-Gen Skins[/b]:[list]                    [*]Vizier Egbert Beakington Ra[/*]                    [*]Court Charmer Aphrodite[/*]                    [*]Court Archer Cupid[/*]                [/list]            [/*]            [*][b]Divine Legacy[/b]: Supernova Pele[/*]            [*][b]New Cosmetics[/b]:[list]                    [*][b]Ninja Vanish[/b] global emote[/*]                    [*][b]Silent Strike[/b] badge[/*]                [/list]            [/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]General Additions[/b]
        [list]            [*][b]HUD Editor[/b](for PC & Console):[list]                    [*]Customize UI layouts.[/*]                    [*]On console, move elements with the right stick.[/*]                [/list]            [/*]            [*][b]Music Packs[/b]:[list]                    [*]Over 60 returning SMITE 1 music packs in a special chest.[/*]                    [*]Equipped via [b]Profile > Loadout[/b].[/*]                    [*][u]Celtic Music Pack[/u] coming free as part of a St. Patrick’s Day event.[/*]                [/list]            [/*]        [/list]    [/*][/list][h2][b]Conquest Map & Game Mode Updates[/b][/h2][b]Conquest Changes[/b][list]    [*]        
[b]Slower Gold Gain[/b]
        [list]            [*]Extends mid-game so you don’t max out builds too fast.[/*]            [*]Makes early and mid-game fights more meaningful before late-game items come online.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Brute Minions[/b]
        [list]            [*]Tankier minions appear after 7 minutes to help break tower defenses.[/*]            [*]Resist mage clears more effectively and remove backdoor protections when they reach structures.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Minion vs. Minion TTK Adjustments[/b]
        [list]            [*]Reduces wave stacking so lanes don’t snowball into huge waves unintentionally.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Fire Minions[/b]
        [list]            [*]No longer grant bonus gold if your Phoenix is down, discouraging excessive turtling.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Towers & Phoenixes[/b]
        [list]            [*]Increased penetration damage for more defensive power.[/*]            [*][b]New Minion Counter[/b] under each tower’s HP bar shows how many allied minions remain.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Runic Bomb Upgrades[/b]
        [list]            [*]Extended throw range with a fun “lob” effect.[/*]            [*]Can now destroy the Fire Giant Pit door (great for strategic firefights).[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Fountain Healing[/b]
        [list]            [*]Now ticks every 0.2s instead of every 1s (same total healing, just smoother).[/*]        [/list]    [/*][/list][h3][b]Joust[/b][/h3][list]    [*][b]Titan Health[/b]: Increased from 10,000 to 12,500 to prevent overly fast Titan kills.[/*][/list][h2][b]God Balance Highlights[/b][/h2][list]    [*][b]Achilles[/b]: Increased cooldown on [b]Combat Dodge[/b] to reduce lane poke/spam.[/*]    [*][b]Bellona[/b]: [b]Bludgeon[/b] damage & [b]Scourge[/b] healing scaled back to reduce lane dominance.[/*]    [*][b]Chaac[/b]: [b]Rain Dance[/b] healing increased, boosting his overall sustain.[/*]    [*][b]Khepri[/b]: Base kit buffed (shorter Solar Flare cooldown); [b]Aspect[/b] damage scaling reduced.[/*]    [*][b]Mordred[/b](Major Adjustments):[list]            [*]Old Shoulder Charge Aspect folded into the base kit (it was too fun to leave as an Aspect only).[/*]            [*][b]Aspect of Rage[/b] reworked to grant cooldown resets on successful basics while Blood Rage is active.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*][b]Rama[/b]: Better base kit damage/duration; [b]Aspect of Precision[/b] toned down (less attack speed).[/*]    [*][b]Thanatos[/b]: Base kit healing & damage scaling improved; [b]Aspect[/b] sees reduced damage/heal.[/*]    [*][b]Thor[/b]: [b]Anvil of Dawn[/b] warning visuals shortened to match SMITE 1 timing, allowing for more consistent surprise ults.[/*]    [*][b]Vulcan[/b]: Passive mods (efficiency & thermal) both buffed for better payoff.[/*]    [*][b]Zeus[/b]: [b]Chain Lightning[/b] damage scaling up for stronger poke.[/*][/list]
[h2][b]Item Balance Updates[/b][/h2][list]    [*]        
[b]Arondite[/b] (New Item)
        [list]            [*]Adds anti-stealth and high-utility scouting (peeking over walls).[/*]            [*]Tailored for ability assassins needing more awareness and burst potential.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Elixirs (Strength & Int)[/b]
        [list]            [*]Curbed power spike in super-late game; toned down subsequent purchases.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Spectral Armor[/b]
        [list]            [*]Heavier attack-speed and crit-chance debuffs to combat high-crit comps.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Void Items[/b] (e.g., Void Stone/Shield)
        [list]            [*]Protection shred decreased from 15% to 12%.[/*]            [*]Bug fixes so the shred applies consistently and fairly.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Stone of Binding[/b]
        [list]            [*]Slightly weaker debuff, but overall more reliable vs. low-protection targets.[/*]            [*]Gained a bit more protective stats.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Devourer’s Gauntlet[/b]
        [list]            [*]Higher Strength per stack (+0.5) to reward fully stacked builds.[/*]        [/list]    [/*]    [*]        
[b]Magi’s Cloak[/b]
        [list]            [*]Cooldown up from 60s to 90s; cost increased by 100 gold.[/*]        [/list]    [/*][/list]

[h2][b]Quality-of-Life & Bug Fixes[/b][/h2][list]    [*][b]Elixir Sound[/b]: Slurps less noisy now![/*]    [*][b]Susano[/b]: Smoothed out the pull timing on Wind Siphon for more consistent targeting.[/*]    [*][b]Floating Combat Text[/b]: Gold/XP, Heal, and Mana text fades faster and matches damage-number style.[/*]    [*][b]Item Store Improvements[/b]:[list]            [*]Clicking empty slots for Starter/Consumable/Relic auto-filters the shop to relevant items.[/*]            [*]If you buy wards or potions mid-build, returning to your partially-built item no longer forgets your Tier 3 path.[/*]            [*]Recommended Items tab is clearer for new players.[/*]        [/list]    [/*][/list][h2][b]Looking Ahead[/b][/h2][list]    [*][b]Ongoing Pacing Tweaks[/b]: Dev team will keep an eye on match lengths, tower pressure, and overall player feedback in both Conquest and non-Conquest modes.[/*]    [*][b]Aspects & Hybrid Roles[/b]: Further refinements expected to balance out bruiser vs. pure-tank vs. damage-focused builds.[/*]    [*][b]Future Patches[/b]: Continued Conquest environment art upgrades, UI enhancements (like multi-filter in the shop), and more new items/features on the way.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Open Beta 5 Now Live! Bari enters the Battle!
notes.content:
Welcome to the SMITE 2: Open Beta 5 update! This update introduces our newest deity, Princess Bari, hailing from the Korean Pantheon. Her unique playstyle revolves around Mystic Surge, granting her powerful burst windows where her abilities have no cooldown and gain special bonus effects. With a versatile kit blending mobility, crowd control, and hybrid scaling, Bari is sure to bring new options to the battlefield.

    We’re also making changes to gameplay and player customization with this update. Conquest receives a significant overhaul to its gold pacing and minion mechanics to encourage more strategic sieging and reduce unexpected snowballing. 

    Meanwhile, we’re introducing a major new feature that many have been asking about! Our HUD Editor which will now give you complete control over your in-game interface! You can now play your way, and set various elements such as scale and opacity. 

    It'll be music to your ears, as we introduce Music Packs from SMITE 1 , allowing you to unlock and personalize your battle soundtrack. Finally, there are plenty of fresh skins and cosmetics up for grabs—don’t miss out on the brand-new Silent Wish Aladdin or the chance to bolster your collection with favorites from SMITE 1’s legacy lineup.

    Dive into the detailed patch notes below for the full rundown on Princess Bari’s abilities, the new HUD customization options, gold pacing changes, and everything else in store for Open Beta 5.

- Music Packs are now in SMITE 2! A variety of god-like soundtracks from SMITE 1 are available for unlock via the Classic Music Chest, purchasable for 100% Legacy Gems! Roll the Chest today and start building out your in game playlist!

tags.balance_change: - Alpha creature base gold reduced by 1g
- Base gold reward for player kills increased from 150g to 200g
- A brute will replace a melee minion in the waves at set intervals throughout the match
- Brutes spawn with an anti-magic shield, making them more resilient to magical damage
- Brutes have more health and power than a normal melee minion
- Minions will now do a consistent amount of damage to each other at all points throughout the match
- Ranged minions will now try to target minotaurs as they move forward passed their normal line formation
- Melee and ranged minions will now attempt to prioritize ranged minions who are standing near the melee line formation
- Fire minions no longer grant bonus gold when slain
- Tier 1 tower penetration increased to 10% to 20%

notes.title: Titan Talks Roundup March 7th
notes.content:
We had a very special Titan Talks yesterday with Isiah, Kilgon, and Max 'Innocent Rabbit'. In this episode, they dove into the complexities of matchmaking and ranked systems, addressing community concerns, upcoming updates, and new competitive formats. They also discussed ranked resets, toxic queues, and the technical work behind offering a balanced gaming experience.

Here is what you missed!
[h2][b]1. Upcoming Update Reminders[/b][/h2][list][*][b]OB5 Launch[/b]: Scheduled for Monday (exact date provided in-stream).[/*][*][b]Patch Notes[/b]:[list][*]Full patch notes go live soon, with a Monday patch overview stream.[/*][*]Includes behind-the-scenes logic on balance changes and bug fixes.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Console vs. PC Parity[/b]:[list][*]All platforms generally receive the same hotfixes and updates, but console patches may be delayed slightly by certification times.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]2. Esports & Community Tournaments[/b][/h2][list][*]
[b]Inbound’s Tournament (“The Bobby Tourney”)[/b]
[list][*]Taking place over the current weekend (after the show date).[/*][*]Features high-level/pro players competing for prize pools sponsored by Hi-Rez.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]EU Tournaments by Nika & Hazer[/b]
[list][*]Scheduled to begin on [b]March 15[/b].[/*][*]Sign-ups require a [b]high-level ranked[/b] standing.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Chris T. Dixon’s Joust Cash Cups[/b]
[list][*]Joust-focused cash prize events.[/*][*]Great opportunity for 3v3 enthusiasts to compete.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Smite Lovers United Tourney[/b]
[list][*]Crowdfunded community tournament with sign-ups open.[/*][*]Additional details available on social media.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Potential Additional Esports Announcement[/b]
[list][*]Teased further reveals after the show.[/*][*]Check [b]@Smite2Esports[/b] Twitter for the latest updates.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]3. Matchmaking & Ranked: Key Updates[/b][/h2]
Max provided a high-level [b]timeline[/b] of matchmaking changes from Closed Beta through Open Beta 4:

[b]3.1 Open Beta 1[/b]
[list][*][b]Match Quality Metric[/b]:[list][*]Combined skill-based (SR) and experience-based data to evaluate potential matches.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Level/SR Ranges[/b]:[list][*]The matchmaker began with a tight range and gradually widened if queues went on too long.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Party Composition Rules[/b]:[list][*]Aim to prevent extreme scenarios (e.g., large premades vs. all solo players).[/*][/list][/*][/list]
[b]3.2 Open Beta 2[/b]
[list][*][b]Team Averages[/b]:[list][*]New check on average player level/SR per team to refine balance.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Backend Skill Ratings[/b]:[list][*]Enhanced how hidden MMR and SR data are used for both casual and ranked matchmaking.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Trio Queue Updates[/b]:[list][*]Adjusted how three-player parties are handled to avoid mismatching them.[/*][/list][/*][/list]
[b]3.3 Open Beta 3[/b]
[list][*][b]New Player Experience & QoL[/b]:[list][*]Focused on UI improvements, pick/ban sound cues to lower accidental lobby abandonments.[/*][*]General bug fixes and improvements rather than direct changes to matchmaking rules.[/*][/list][/*][/list]
[b]3.4 Open Beta 4[/b]
[list][*][b]Final Lobby Rule Adherence[/b]:[list][*]Prevented outliers (e.g., very high-SR players waiting too long) from warping all in-progress matches.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Soft Capping Top Players[/b]:[list][*]Ensures top SR players (e.g., 6000 SR) match with similar-level opponents faster, rather than waiting extreme lengths or diluting other matches.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]4. Current Priorities & Future Plans[/b][/h2][olist][*]
[b]Logical Team Balance[/b]
[list][*]Seeking ways to ensure that if two big skill outliers are in the same lobby, they end up on the correct teams.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Top-Ranked Experience[/b]
[list][*]Want high-level matches (e.g., top 0.1% of players) to be more consistent in quality and skill parity.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Exploring Alternate Matchmaking Styles[/b]
[list][*]Potentially combining “count-up” (current style) with a “countdown” approach for top-tier players.[/*][*]Looking back at SMITE 1’s systems for inspirations or hybrid solutions.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]New Player Experience[/b]
[list][*]Improve how true newcomers are introduced and avoid them being matched against far more experienced players.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]New Competitive Formats[/b]
[list][*]Additional modes or tournament-style features are “in the works.”[/*][*]Could offer more serious (or alternative) competition without overly fragmenting the existing player base.[/*][/list][/*][/olist][h2][b]5. Q&A Highlights[/b][/h2][list][*]
[b]Why Not Hard-Cap SR Differences?[/b]
[list][*]Off-peak times and lower population hours cause severe queue times for players, especially at high SR extremes (e.g., 14+ minute waits).[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Casual vs. Ranked Matchmaking[/b]
[list][*][b]Casual[/b]: Primarily level- and hidden-MMR-based; can broaden quickly to reduce wait times.[/*][*][b]Ranked[/b]: Stricter SR constraints initially, then expands to ensure players find matches before leaving queue.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Party Size & Skill Gaps[/b]
[list][*]Technical limitations currently prevent restricting parties by SR gaps.[/*][*]Planned future improvements to limit wide SR gaps in parties (e.g., 2500+ SR differences).[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Ranked Rewards[/b]
[list][*][b]God Borders[/b] tied to ranked achievements are planned as a key reward.[/*][*]Additional incentives in development; details coming later in the season.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Individual Performance in Ranked[/b]
[list][*]In-game performance metrics (KDA, gold, damage) can be misleading.[/*][*]Risk of incentivizing “bad behaviors” (e.g., farming stats in a lost game).[/*][*]Devs remain open to possibilities but want to avoid damaging the competitive ecosystem.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]More Leaderboards & Tracking[/b]
[list][*]Enhanced backend support coming, which could enable worshiper leaderboards or other ranking formats.[/*][*]Front-end UI/time is needed to display these properly.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Console Update Delays[/b]
[list][*]Typically minor, due to platform certification requirements.[/*][*]Server-side fixes often arrive simultaneously on all platforms.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]6. Closing Thoughts[/b][/h2][list][*][b]OB5 Patch[/b]: Releasing Monday, featuring various updates and a patch overview show.[/*][*][b]Community Engagement[/b]: Encouraged to watch or participate in ongoing tournaments and keep an eye on SMITE 2 Esports social channels for more announcements.[/*][*][b]Future Titan Talks[/b]: More info on new competitive modes and further matchmaking improvements will be discussed in upcoming shows.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Titan Talks March 5th and Hotfix Roundup
notes.content:
Welcome to another edition of [b]Titan Talk[/b], wherew we chat all things [b]SMITE 2[/b]: new updates, behind-the-scenes development tidbits, upcoming events, and community questions. Below is a quick-look summary of key highlights! [h2] [/h2][h2]1. Hotfix & Xbox Rollback[/h2][list][*]A recent [b]hotfix[/b] went out addressing a few issues:[list][*][b]Poseidon’s Passive[/b]: Fixed a bug where Poseidon’s Changing Tides movement speed wasn’t applying.[/*][*][b]Awilix Fixes[/b]:[list][*]Flip-over mechanic no longer causes you to get stuck.[/*][*]Gravity Surge no longer drops targets into walls.[/*][*]Adjusted certain hit/attack timings to make her feel smoother to play.[/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][b]Xbox Rollback[/b]: A build rollback occurred to fix an Xbox update download issue. While this means redownloading for some players, the team felt it was the quickest way to restore stable play for everyone.[/*][/list][h2]2. HUD Editor Update[/h2][list][*][b]Coming in OB5[/b]: A new, more flexible HUD editor.[/*][*][b]Controller Support[/b]: Initially believed to be PC-only, the team confirmed it [u]will[/u] work on controller as well.[/*][*][b]Easy Customization[/b]: Arrange in-game elements using the right stick (on console). The team aims to give players on all platforms the freedom to personalize their interface.[/*][/list][h2]3. Upcoming Tournament[/h2][list][*][b]Community Event[/b]: Bobby “Inbowned” is hosting a weekend tournament featuring top players, ex-pros, and well-known streamers.[/*][*][b]9,000 USD Prize Pool[/b]: Sponsored by Hi-Rez. Expect high-level SMITE 2 games with popular names like FineOkay, RatMilk, Ducky, Clumsy, and more.[/*][*][b]Where to Watch[/b]: Tune into Inbowned’s channel and participating players’ streams this weekend.[/*][/list][h2]4. OB5 Teasers & Planned Content[/h2][list][*][b]Princess Bari[/b]: Our newest carry/mage-hybrid god introduced in OB5. Her ascended form grants her basic attacks splash damage, making her a formidable DPS option.[/*][*][b]Item & Aspect Adjustments[/b]:[list][*][b]Pridwen[/b] arriving in Week 2 of OB5.[/*][*]Various existing Aspects (like Mordred, Sobek, Fenrir) are getting tweaks.[/*][*]Mordred’s ultimate wind-up can now rotate the camera so you can keep aiming while charging it.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]5. Hot Topics & Community Q&A Highlights[/h2] Below is a quick rundown of the biggest talking points during the Q&A portion: [h3]Matchmaking & Ranked[/h3][list][*]Ongoing [b]matchmaking improvements[/b]: More back-end updates are in the works, and the team will share details on Friday with Max (Innocent Rabbit).[/*][*]The devs are continuously adjusting variables to improve match quality for both solo and party players.[/*][/list][h3]Store, Gifting, & Cosmetics[/h3][list][*][b]Music Packs[/b] now available primarily via chests; more distribution methods may come as the in-game store develops.[/*][*][b]Cross-Gen Skins[/b]: More are becoming available each update; if you’re missing any from SMITE 1, logging into SMITE 1 first sometimes forces them to sync.[/*][*][b]Gifting[/b]: Not prioritized right now due to fraud concerns and dev time constraints.[/*][/list][h3]Console-Specific Notes[/h3][list][*][b]HUD Editor[/b] confirmed functional on controllers in OB5.[/*][*][b]Aim Assist[/b]: SMITE 1’s console aim assist was off by default due to many players preferring manual aiming. The team is exploring improved tech but not committing yet.[/*][*][b]Store Improvements[/b]: Expect a cleaner item shop with better flow, grid views for consumables/relics, and overall smoother navigation.[/*][/list]

General Features & Future Plans

[list][*][b]Wandering Market[/b] repeats every ~8 weeks: You can keep old markets active and collect coins over time.[/*][*][b]Text Chat on Console[/b]: Blocked by lengthy certification steps, but devs will work toward it later.[/*][*][b]God Builder[/b]: Actively in development. It’s surprisingly complex (covering multiple UI screens, integrations, and backend).[/*][/list][h2]6. Welcome to another Titan Talk! We’re excited to share the latest news on [u]SMITE 2[/u], including the reveal of our newest Goddess and several important updates that just went live (or are coming soon). Here’s a quick breakdown:
[h2][b]1. New Goddess: Princess Bari[/b][/h2][list][*]
[b]First Korean Pantheon God[/b]
[list][*][b]Lore[/b]: Princess Bari was the unwanted seventh daughter who ultimately descended into the underworld to save her dying father. Despite being unappreciated, her selflessness and compassion led her to ascend into divinity.[/*][*][b]Theme & Aesthetics[/b]: Bari blends elements of Korean shamanic tradition—her signature bell staff, ceremonial fan, and distinctive wide-brimmed hat all reflect real-world Korean shamanism motifs.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Gameplay Role & Overview[/b]
[list][*][b]Magical Carry or Mage[/b]: She deals [u]magical[/u] damage but can flex into mid or duo.[/*][*][b]Unique Resource – Spirit[/b][list][*]Builds from attacking gods or minions.[/*][*]Reaching 100 Spirit triggers a brief “Mystic Surge,” granting bonus stats and one [u]enhanced[/u] cast of an ability.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Abilities[/b]:[olist][*][b]Sacred Bell[/b] – Throws a bell projectile that can later be knocked around or pulled back to Bari, dealing damage (and eventually stunning when enhanced).[/*][*][b]Warding Gust[/b] – A fan-swipe in a cone. Knocks back enemies who are too close. Can also ricochet or empower the thrown bell.[/*][*][b]Reverent Steps[/b] – A freeform dance step dash that fires a projectile at the end; hitting an enemy god grants a burst of Spirit and reduces cooldown.[/*][*][b]Ultimate: Spirit’s Cadence[/b][list][*]Summons an area-of-effect dance that applies a short, “cheat-death” style protection to Bari and any allies who stand inside it.[/*][*]Instantly fills Bari’s Spirit to 100 and extends her “Mystic Surge,” giving her bonus attack speed, AoE basic attacks, and an enhanced ability cast.[/*][*]Protected allies who would drop to zero HP become briefly damage-immune (but silenced/disarmed). Executes still override this effect.[/*][/list][/*][/olist][/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Playstyle Tips[/b]
[list][*][b]Combo Potential[/b]: Juggle the bells effectively for crowd control, wave clear, or burst damage.[/*][*][b]Team Fight Power[/b]: The Ultimate provides a lifesaving zone and re-empowers Bari for big plays.[/*][*][b]Build Paths[/b]: Lean into more “carry” style (Strength) for bigger basic attacks, or “mage” style (Intelligence) for heavy ability damage.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]2. Recent & Upcoming Game Updates[/b][/h2][list][*]
[b]Awilix Release[/b]
[list][*][u]Awilix[/u] is now live in [u]SMITE 2[/u], offering a Jaguar-riding assassin playstyle. Enjoy riding Suku into battle and more new plus-one abilities.[/*][/list][/*][*]

[list][*]PC players can now cap framerate at 90 or 144 FPS. More options could be added if there’s demand—give your feedback![/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Double Worshiper Event[/b]
[list][*]A minor technical delay meant the Double Worshiper Weekend started late. To compensate, the event is extended for an extra day so everyone can level up their new gods.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Minor Fixes & Hotfixes[/b]
[list][*][b]Draft Lobby Display[/b]: An issue causing hidden team names in draft lobbies was fixed.[/*][*][b]Magi’s Cloak Bug[/b]: Coming soon (or already hotfixed) to fix random procs.[/*][*][b]Thor Aspect Changes[/b]: Some slow/cleanse tweaks and healing reductions are on the way.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]New Item: Erendite[/b]
[list][*]Returning as an [u]active[/u] item featuring a stealth-reveal ability (think a “sonar ping” effect).[/*][*]Successful reveals grant bonus damage and movement speed for a chase.[/*][*]Perfect for countering invisible gods like Loki or Izanami.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]HUD Editor (PC Beta)[/b]
[list][*]A long-awaited feature is here: you can now move and resize HUD elements freely on PC.[/*][*]Console support planned for a future update once the PC version is polished.[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Music Packs[/b]
[list][*]60+ classic music themes from past events, passes, and more are returning in a Music Chest.[/*][*]Use your Legacy Gems to roll for these nostalgic themes (excluding licensed tracks).[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Conquest & Other Balance Tweaks[/b]
[list][*]Refinements to Conquest map visuals near towers.[/*][*]Further Aspect adjustments are in development—stay tuned for official patch notes.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]3. What’s Next[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Flash Testing[/b]: Princess Bari and these newest changes should be available in Flash Testing very soon. Jump in, try them out, and leave feedback.[/*][*][b]Keep the Feedback Coming[/b]: Let us know on the official forums, social channels, and in-game bug reports what you think about Bari, Erendite, HUD Editor, and more.[/*][*][b]Stay Tuned for More Gods[/b]: We’re continuing to refine and update existing characters, plus new additions are always in the works![/*][/list]
[b]Thanks for reading this week’s Titan Talk summary![/b] We can’t wait for everyone to try out [u]Princess Bari[/u], experiment with the new item [u]Erendite[/u], and enjoy all the quality-of-life updates.

notes.title: Princess Bari: A Closer Look
notes.content:
Princess Bari    

The Divine Mudang

Pantheon : Korean

    Gameplay Specializations:
[list]    [*]        Ranged    [/*]    [*]        Magical Damage    [/*]    [*]        Strength & Intelligence Hybrid    [/*]    [*]        Explosive Moments of Power    [/*]    [*]        Death Prevention    [/*][/list]
    “When all others turn away, the abandoned child carries hope on her shoulders.”
[h2]            Who is Princess Bari?    [/h2]
    Born as the seventh daughter to a king who longed only for a male heir, Princess Bari[b] [/b]was cast aside at birth—deemed unworthy by her own family. When her father fell gravely ill, however, it was Bari who journeyed across mortal and spirit realms to obtain the divine waters needed to restore his life. 

    This act of profound selflessness not only healed her father but also bestowed Bari with divine power. Now a powerful shaman, she stands as a guiding light between the living and the dead. She harnesses her gifts to protect the vulnerable and uphold the delicate balance of both realms.

    In SMITE 2, Princess Bari uses her ever-growing reservoir of spiritual energy to amplify her abilities. Each strike or ability she lands builds up her Spirit, fueling a cycle of enhanced attacks and spells that demonstrate her merciful but resolute nature.

           [h2] New Pantheon – Korean    [/h2]

    With the arrival of Princess Bari, SMITE proudly welcomes the Korean Pantheon. While there were countless figures we could have introduced, Princess Bari stands out as one of the most iconic and universally cherished characters in Korean mythology.  With her introduction we pay homage to her enduring legacy in Korean mythology and shine a light on a story of deep compassion, resilience, and divine miracles that still captures many to this day.

     [h2]       Core Themes    [/h2]

    [b]Edge of Life and Death[/b]
    As a spiritual shaman, Princess Bari treads the fine line between both realms. Her kit revolves around collecting Spirit and entering an enhanced Spiritual State, mirroring her role as a soul guide and caretaker.

     [h2]       Supporting Themes    [/h2]

    [b]Altruistic Protector[/b]
    Although she can deal formidable damage, Bari also stands as a protective figure who can spare allies from death and tip the scales of battle in her team’s favor.

    [b]Bell Magic & Ritual Dances[/b]
    Iconic bells and graceful ritual dances form the heart of Princess Bari’s combat style. She conjures bells on the battlefield, then sends them forward at her foes. Her rituals bring not only strong protective capabilities but enhance her own strength, giving her clear moments of power unique to her.
           
[h2] Artistic Process  [/h2] 
 
    For Princess Bari, we wanted to highlight her deep connection to Korean Shamanistic traditions. Her color palette draws heavily from the Sam-Taegeuk symbol, a core emblem in many shamanic practices. We emphasized key ritual items—her hat, fan, and bangul (a bell-bearing staff)—both in her visual design and her gameplay mechanics.

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/Bari_1_59773374ad.png[/img]

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/Bari_2_dc0f97da06.png[/img]

    Animation-wise, our goal was to make her movements fluid and graceful, as though she were dancing across the battlefield. Wherever possible, we aimed to display this grace—be it in her idle animations, recalling sequences, or core combat abilities.

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/image_9174aa2082.png[/img]

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/bari_3d_c648ff2334.jpg[/img]

    Princess Bari stands between the realms of life and death, and her abilities reflect this duality. In her normal state, they feel more physical and incorporate gold and blue hues. However, when she enters her Spiritual state, the palette shifts to a ghostly blend of blue, white, and negative space. We wanted this transformation to be dramatic and easily recognizable, so we built up a visual crescendo before she bursts into her Spiritual form, as shown below.

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/Highres_Screenshot00004_c1f1aedea7.png[/img]
           
[h2] Gameplay    [/h2]

    Princess Bari’s gameplay centers on [b]Spirit[/b]—she does not use Mana, but instead accumulates Spirit with each successful hit or ability cast. Upon reaching the Spirit threshold, Princess Bari surges with power, amplifying her damage, enhancing her abilities, and granting special effects to her basic attacks.

    Princess Bari conjures bells, tossing them into the fray to damage and disrupt her enemies. She sweeps them forward with a graceful fan flourish, weaving each strike into a fluid combo that builds her Spirit. Drawing on protective rituals, Princess Bari protects allies from lethal harm while fueling her own surge of power. She enters a heightened state that amplifies her next attack, choosing the right one for the situation.
    
    [b]Unique Gameplay Features[/b]
[list]    [*]        Princess Bari is a Hybrid god, excelling at the traditional carry role through Strength while being a more flexible caster with Intelligence.    [/*]    [*]        Combo-centric kit, with a variety of ways to approach each fight depending on her current Spirit and her goals in the fight    [/*]    [*]        Ebb and Flow of Power. Princess Bari excels at transitioning from her Physical and Spiritual forms, gaining access to extra cooldown usages and powerful bonuses.    [/*]    [*]        Teamwide Death Immunity, allies simply need to be part of her Ritual to gain this potent effect.    [/*][/list]           

[h2] Closing    [/h2]

    Whether you’re conjuring bells to zone out enemies or safeguarding your teammates with life-saving rituals, Bari’s skill ceiling rewards ingenuity and careful Spirit management. Guide your allies from harm’s edge, and stand as Princess Bari—the guide between realms.

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/Bari_Splash_web_f4532bd5a1.jpg[/img]

tags.feature: With the arrival of Princess Bari, SMITE proudly welcomes the Korean Pantheon.

notes.title: Titan Talks and Hotfix Roundup March 1st
notes.content:
[h2]Technical Updates & Hotfixes[/h2]
[b]Hotfixes That Went Live[/b]
[list][*]
[b]Double Worshippers Event:[/b] Talked about an issue affecting the event but this has been resolved. 
[/*][*]
[b]Recent Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]
[b]Assault Bench Issue:[/b] Resolved a problem where initial picks were getting incorrectly added to the bench.
[/*][*]
[b]Auto Build Upgrades:[/b] Starter item upgrades now functioning as intended.
[/*][*]
[b]Spirit of Desolation / Jotun’s Revenge:[/b] Will no longer proc on clones.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Prophetic Cloak Reactivation:[/b] Prophetic Cloak was turned back on after the devs ironed out some unexpected behaviors.
[/*][*]
[b]Typhon’s Fang Disabled:[/b] Temporarily removed because buying and selling it retained its passive permanently. A fix is on the way.
[/*][/list][h2]God Release Roadmap[/h2]
[b]Overview[/b]
[list][*]
The SMITE 2 team is moving toward a [b]new God release schedule[/b]: [b]one God every two weeks[/b] rather than every week. This begins with the next new God, [b]Princess Bari[/b], on [b]March 10[/b].
[/*][*]
[b]Additional Weekly Content:[/b] Though God releases switch to bi-weekly, there will still be new aspects, items, and other exciting gameplay content [b]every week[/b].
[/*][*]
The new schedule: [b]five classic Gods[/b] followed by [b]an all-new God[/b], ensuring a steady stream of beloved favorites and fresh faces.
[/*][/list]
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/44832142/a7487e0bc9ba3a3822f4d0d9ac4dbb41df896b66.png[/img]
[b]Upcoming God Dates (Subject to Change)[/b]
[olist][*]
[b]Princess Bari[/b] – March 10 (OB 5)
[/*][*]
[b]Merlin[/b] – March 24 (OB 6)
[/*][*]
[b]Cerberus[/b] – April 7
[/*][*]
[b]Kali[/b] – April 21
[/*][*]
[b]Guan Yu[/b] – May 5
[/*][*]
[b]Apollo[/b] – May 19
[/*][*]
[b]New God (H)[/b] – June 2
[/*][/olist]
[b]Why the Change?[/b]
[list][*]
[b]Quality & Pace:[/b] The dev team wants to ensure each God has the level of polish and testing required for a stellar release.
[/*][*]
[b]Production Realities:[/b] After recent team restructuring, it’s important to maintain a sustainable production cadence.
[/*][*]
[b]Community Feedback:[/b] Many players requested more time to adapt to each new God, so this schedule supports that.
[/*][/list][h2]Art Deep Dive: Upcoming Gods[/h2]
Art Director [b]Ben[/b] walked through the unique challenges of bringing each God into SMITE 2’s upgraded engine:
[h3]1. Princess Bari[/h3][list][*]
[b]Pantheon:[/b] The first [b]Korean[/b] deity in SMITE 2, inspired by Korean shamanistic tradition.
[/*][*]
[b]Design Elements:[/b]
[list][*]
Traditional garb (including a culturally-accurate tall hat) and bright pops of color.
[/*][*]
Elaborate bells that tie into her in-game abilities.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Ben’s Notes:[/b]
[list][*]
The team did in-depth cultural research and collaborated with Korean staff to ensure authenticity.
[/*][*]
Vibrant materials show off SMITE 2’s new rendering capabilities.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]2. Merlin[/h3][list][*]
[b]Release Date:[/b] March 24
[/*][*]
[b]Famous for:[/b] Multi-stance magic (Arcane, Fire, Ice).
[/*][*]
[b]Art Challenges:[/b]
[list][*]
Essentially [b]three separate effects sets[/b] for each stance, making it a more complex project.
[/*][*]
Cloth materials and magical accents are enhanced with next-gen PBR (Physically Based Rendering) materials.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Ben’s Notes:[/b]
[list][*]
The original Merlin design was well-received in SMITE 1, so the focus is on polishing visuals and materials.
[/*][*]
Effects teams are creating stand-out animations for each elemental stance.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]3. Cerberus[/h3][list][*]
[b]Release Date:[/b] April 7
[/*][*]
[b]Key Feature:[/b] Three-headed design requires specialized rigging.
[/*][*]
[b]Art Upgrades:[/b]
[list][*]
Adjusted the snout/head ratio to feel more dog-like and balanced.
[/*][*]
Upgraded materials for more realistic and menacing texture details.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Ben’s Notes:[/b]
[list][*]
Each head moves independently, which increases animation complexity.
[/*][*]
Cerberus has unique rigging to handle multi-head behaviors.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]4. Kali[/h3][list][*]
[b]Release Date:[/b] April 21
[/*][*]
[b]Notable Update:[/b] Received a bigger visual overhaul compared to her SMITE 1 design.
[/*][*]
[b]Art Changes:[/b]
[list][*]
No more high-heeled armor; a more culturally resonant mid-ground between classic and modern styles.
[/*][*]
Added a skull garland to highlight her lore roots.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Ben’s Notes:[/b]
[list][*]
The team aims to respect the spirit of Kali’s mythology while balancing modernization.
[/*][*]
Extra arms, new cloth physics, and potential future touches (like a signature tongue cameo) are under consideration.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]5. Guan Yu[/h3][list][*]
[b]Release Date:[/b] May 5
[/*][*]
[b]Core Theme:[/b] Legendary Chinese general vibe intact, with signature armor and horse.
[/*][*]
[b]Visual Tweaks:[/b]
[list][*]
Updates to his horse’s proportions (less “buff,” more realistic form).
[/*][*]
Polished materials to capture the PBR advantages.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Ben’s Notes:[/b]
[list][*]
No major design overhaul; Guan Yu’s stylized look is iconic.
[/*][*]
Might subtly adjust proportions (hand size, etc.) if tech allows.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]6. Apollo[/h3][list][*]
[b]Release Date:[/b] May 19
[/*][*]
[b]Rework Approach:[/b] Largely retains his known SMITE 1 revamp, upgraded with SMITE 2’s advanced materials.
[/*][*]
[b]Ben’s Notes:[/b]
[list][*]
Key goal is to emphasize his golden details and skin rendering.
[/*][*]
Adding subtle finishing touches to ensure cloth, gold, and hair all shine.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][h3]7. Mystery “H” God[/h3][list][*]
[b]Release Date:[/b] June 2
[/*][*]
[b]All-New God[/b]: Expect fresh lore, visuals, and kit design. More details soon!
[/*][/list][h2]Q&A Highlights[/h2]
During the show, [b]Kilgoon[/b] and [b]Ben[/b] fielded community questions on art, design philosophies, and future content:
[olist][*]
[b]Why Bi-Weekly God Releases?[/b]
[list][*]
[b]Quality control[/b] is the main focus. The SMITE 2 team wants every God to feel polished and well-tested.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Collaboration Skins:[/b]
[list][*]
Potential [b]crossover skins[/b] are still on the table for the future, but the team is balancing new productions with community priorities.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Revamping Older Designs:[/b]
[list][*]
The devs aim to maintain each God’s [b]iconic identity[/b] while applying a [b]next-gen art pass[/b] to materials, lighting, and proportions.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Community Concept Submissions:[/b]
[list][*]
The team loves seeing fan-made concepts. If the community responds well, there’s a chance those ideas can become official.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Art & Lore Balance:[/b]
[list][*]
While the team respects the pantheons and their lore, [b]practical gameplay needs[/b] can shift certain design elements.
[/*][*]
Ultimately, the [b]goal is fun[/b], with a nod to authenticity whenever possible.
[/*][/list][/*][/olist][h2]Closing Thoughts[/h2][list][*]
[b]SMITE 2[/b] continues to evolve and refine its gods, giving both veterans and newcomers something to be excited about.
[/*][*]
[b]Community Feedback[/b]: The devs are actively reading and incorporating suggestions, so keep sharing your thoughts.
[/*][*]
[b]Upcoming Streams[/b]: Look out for more Titan Talks and dev shows where they’ll dive deeper into [b]Princess Bari’s[/b] kit, new feature reveals, and eSports updates.
[/*][/list]
[b]Stay tuned for[/b] more Titan Talk episodes as SMITE 2 marches forward with a new content schedule, improved visuals, and community-driven improvements!

Thank you for reading, and we’ll see you on the Battleground of the Gods! Remember to follow our official channels for the latest news and patch updates:

notes.title: Titan Talks and Hotfix Roundup February 27th
notes.content:
Here is what you may have missed over the last 24 hours. First up a quick summary of yesterday's Titan Talk where Isiah and Kilgoon went over a ton of in development and upcoming features and content!
[b]Upcoming Events & Developer Roadmap[/b][list][*]
[b]Friday (Feb 28):[/b] A roadmap update featuring the next wave of God releases and content cadence.
[/*][*]
[b]Monday (Mar 3):[/b] Full reveal of [b]Princess Bari[/b], including a kit breakdown by Pon.
[/*][*]
[b]Future Guest Appearances:[/b] Upcoming episodes will feature Kellen and Ben discussing art and game direction.
[/*][/list][b]Recent Hotfixes & Bug Fixes[/b]
Multiple patches have been rolled out over the last 48 hours, addressing key issues:
[list][*]
[b]General Fixes:[/b]
[list][*]
Aladdin’s [b]AO2[/b] canceling consistency improved.
[/*][*]
[b]Bloodforge[/b] re-added to the item shop.

[/*][*]

[/*][*]
Missing descriptions for recent balance changes added.
[/*][*]
[b]Meditation relic[/b] now functions correctly in Assault.
[/*][*]
Artemis’s [b]non-aspect traps[/b] now stack correctly.
[/*][*]
[b]Xbox crash fix[/b] deployed based on player reports.
[/*][*]
[b]Thor’s Health War Hammer[/b] missing VFX issue is under investigation.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][b]Community Q&A Highlights[/b][list][*]
[b]VGS Issues:[/b] Developers are investigating recent issues with the VGS system. Additional player reports are welcome.
[/*][*]
[b]Classic Skin Pricing:[/b] Classic skins were previously at a sale price. The new pricing reflects intended long-term value.
[/*][*]
[b]Wandering Market Expansion:[/b] Unlikely to exceed four pages due to balance between value and pricing.
[/*][*]
[b]God Token Adjustments:[/b] More God tokens will be added as the roster expands beyond level 50.
[/*][*]
[b]Co-op AI Enhancements:[/b]
[list][*]
Easy AI is being tuned for new players.
[/*][*]
Medium and Hard difficulties are in development.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Godbuilder:[/b] Not included in the next update but remains a work in progress.
[/*][*]
[b]Item Store UI Improvements:[/b]
[list][*]
Upcoming update will make consumables easier to access.
[/*][*]
Rebuilding items will be faster with improved UI recall features.
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Role Assignment Feedback:[/b] Developers are reviewing the matchmaking algorithm to ensure fair distribution of primary role preferences.
[/*][*]
[b]Ward Placement Incentives:[/b] The team is considering adding gold rewards or other incentives for warding.
[/*][*]
[b]Ascension Pass Changes:[/b] No immediate plans to extend beyond level 10, but future updates may re-evaluate this system.
[/*][/list][b]Game Mechanics & Balance Discussions[/b][list][*]
[b]Magi’s Cloak:[/b] Fix incoming for unintended activations (e.g., Ymir’s Rocket Jump breaking his own bubble).
[/*][*]
[b]Anti-Proxy Tech:[/b] Developers are collecting feedback on potential adjustments after the initial wave of changes.
[/*][*]
[b]Displacement Interactions:[/b] Awilix’s interactions with CC and knockups are under review.
[/*][*]
[b]Denying Minions (Dota-style):[/b] The team believes this mechanic does not align with [u]Smite 2’s[/u] action-oriented gameplay.
[/*][*]
[b]Polymorph Abilities:[/b] More gods with polymorph mechanics could be introduced in the future.
[/*][*]
[b]Death Animations Visibility:[/b] The idea of showing death animations only to the defeated player is under consideration.
[/*][/list][b]Technical & Quality of Life Updates[/b][list][*]
[b]UI Fixes:[/b] A fix for the [b]map overlaying the item shop[/b] issue is still in progress.
[/*][*]
[b]Feedback Link in Game:[/b] Bug reported and being addressed.
[/*][*]
[b]Party System Improvement Request:[/b] Developers will review automatic removal of players who close the game.
[/*][*]
[b]Accolades Screen:[/b] Accolades are being tracked and a display system is planned for a future update.
[/*][*]
[b]DLSS & FSR Anti-Aliasing:[/b] DLSS currently requires TAA, but the team is discussing potential improvements with NVIDIA.
[/*][/list[b]Cosmetic & Monetization Discussions[/b][list][*]
[b]Bringing Back Classic Tier 5 Skins:[/b] Unlikely in their full form, but individual transformations from older skins may return as separate cosmetics.
[/*][*]
[b]Multi-Queue Option for Smaller Regions:[/b] Not currently in development, but matchmaking improvements are a priority.
[/*][*]
[b]Store UI Changes:[/b]
[list][*]
No plans to revert to the split item store from early [u]Smite 2[/u] testing.
[/*][*]
Featured store skins will remain curated, with the God tab providing full lists.
[/*][/list][/*][/list][b]New Gods & Content Pipeline[/b][list][*]
[b]New God Release Cadence:[/b]
[list][*]
The roadmap for upcoming gods will be revealed Friday.
[/*][*]
[b]Awilix[/b] is expected to launch Monday (Feb 24).
[/*][/list][/*][*]
[b]Community Influence on God Choices:[/b]
[list][*]
The team prioritizes gods based on player interest and long-term game design.
[/*][*]
The development pipeline takes ~6 months per new god.
[/*][/list][/*][/list[b]Future Thematic & Pantheon Expansions[/b][list][*]
[b]New Conquest Map Theme:[/b] Developers are open to expanding beyond Greek themes but recognize the importance of consistency.
[/*][*]
[b]Pantheon vs. Pantheon Theming:[/b] A possibility for future game modes but requires careful execution.
[/*][*]
[b]Folklore & Literature Characters:[/b] While some characters like [b]Aladdin[/b] and [b]Cthulhu[/b] fit, more modern figures (e.g., Dracula, Robin Hood) remain under discussion.
[/*][*]
[b]Wendigo & Other Dark Folklore:[/b] The team is cautious about adding figures with sensitive cultural origins.
[/*][/list][b]Final Notes & Looking Ahead[/b][list][*]
The next Titan Talk on [b]Friday, February 28[/b], will cover [b]upcoming Gods, content roadmap, and game art discussion with Ben[/b].
[/*][*]
[b]Monday, March 3rd[/b], will feature [b]Princess Bari’s full gameplay reveal[/b].
[/*][*]
Keep sharing feedback on [b]Titan Talk, Discord, and bug report forums[/b]!
[/*][/list]

We don't want to forgot about the small hotfix we pushed out!

notes.content:
[h1]SMITE 2: Titan Talk Recap (February 24, 2025)[/h1]
Isiah and Kilgun were there for another edition of Titan Talk as they dive into the latest updates from Open Beta 4, including the new gods, items, and aspects. They addressed player feedback, discussed current issues like Blood Forge and Meditation in Assault mode, and provided insights on the recent updates. Here is what you missed!

notes.title: Open Beta 4 is Now Live!
notes.content:
Welcome to our Open Beta 4 update! This patch features the highly anticipated return of Artemis from SMITE 1—reimagined and ready to conquer the battleground in SMITE 2.

    [img]https://webcdn.hirezstudios.com/smite2-cdn/Artemis_Default_V4_Splash_1920x1080_c4a38e3c6b.jpg[/img]

    We also have a fresh lineup of Cross-Gen and Classic skins making their way into the store, including Foxy Amaterasu, Baron Frostchild Ymir, La Roca Hercules, Summer Fun Medusa, Hellforged Thor, Lil Bites Sobek, and Nano-Mancer Baron Samedi. Some of these skins can be purchased with Legacy Gems, while the Boss Man Danzaburou skin returns as a Divine Legacy unlock for those who earned it in SMITE 1.

    Thor is also receiving a brand-new Aspect, allowing players to alter the God of Thunder’s gameplay for a truly unique experience. If you haven’t played him awhile, it might be time to put him back in the rotation.

    Looking ahead, Awilix is set to arrive on March 3, bringing her dynamic combat style to the roster. Dive into the details below to learn more about these major additions—alongside the extensive balance changes, quality-of-life improvements, and bug fixes that round out this update. Strap in and prepare for the next phase of SMITE 2’s open beta!

notes.title: SMITE 2 Titan Talks and Hotfix Roundup February 22nd
notes.content:
Here is a quick recap from anything you missed yesterday! 

[h1] Titan Talks February 21st[/h1]

[h2] [b]Why Release OB4 on a Monday?[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Avoiding Weekend Hotfixes:[/b] The dev team prefers early-week launches to ensure they’re fully staffed and ready to address any immediate post-patch issues. Launching late in the week risks weekend problems—and weekend work for the team.[/*][*][b]Watch Socials for Timing:[/b] While 7:00 AM Eastern was the targeted downtime, final live times vary. Once servers are updated, official channels will announce when OB4 is truly playable.[/*][/list][h2] [b]New God & Aspect Strategy[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Artemis’s Aspect Arrives Immediately[/b][list][*]The team noted it’s interesting to see players get used to a god’s base kit before introducing a transformative Aspect. Despite launching Artemis’s Aspect right away this time, expect future gods to release their Aspects [u]later[/u] to allow players more time on the base kit first.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Awilix’s Visual & Kit Approach[/b][list][*]Devs wanted to preserve her fluid “flow-state” playstyle, adding only small tweaks (e. g., synergy with Suku). Feedback from early tests suggested any drastic revamp would break her core feel. Hence, her OB4 design changes focus on thematic flourish rather than a big mechanical shift.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2] [b]Face Model Updates & Art Consistency[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Community Feedback:[/b] Achilles, Aphrodite, and Poseidon (Phantom Seas) got revised face/rigging to closer match their card art.[/*][*][b]Intent:[/b] Card art and in-game models should align more faithfully, so the team is constantly fine-tuning lighting, rigging, and facial geometry based on feedback.[/*][/list][h2] [b]Assault “Team Bench” & Reroll Philosophy[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Addressing “I Wanted That God!”[/b][list][*]Players have long been frustrated when a teammate rerolls a god they actually wanted. Now, once rerolled, that “discarded” god goes to a shared “Team Bench.” Anyone can pick it up, keeping the random fun alive but reducing lost opportunities.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Maintaining Random Spirit[/b][list][*]Devs don’t want Assault to become a free-choice mode. Healers are still limited, and only rerolled gods appear on the bench. They’ll watch how this new system affects team comps and match pacing.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2] [b]Conquest Changes: The Bigger Picture[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Encouraging Early Aggression[/b][list][*]The team noticed that farming could feel strictly better than fighting early. XP from kills is now more rewarding, making early ganks and aggression a viable path to victory.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Diminishing Returns on Bullying[/b][list][*]When a high-level player repeatedly kills a much lower-level player, the XP gained is noticeably reduced. The goal is to avoid the “snowball effect” of hammering an under-leveled opponent for the same big reward.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Doors, Minotaurs & Base Sieges[/b][list][*][b]Runic Bomb[/b] can now destroy enemy base doors; minotaurs remain strong tools for closing out the game. The devs hope these tweaks encourage more dynamic endgame pushes and coordinate objective-based play.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2] [b]UI & Quality of Life: Rationale Behind the Updates[/b][/h2][list][*][b]Scoreboard Ability Details[/b][list][*]Newer players struggled to understand an enemy’s abilities after dying. Being able to hover or select an enemy god’s portrait to read their kit helps reduce confusion and fosters better counterplay.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]God Page Refinements[/b][list][*]Multi-stance gods can toggle through stance abilities directly in the god page. This was highly requested in Titan Talk sessions for clarity and practice outside of live matches.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Jump Stamp Visibility[/b][list][*]Previously, jump stamps were visible through Fog of War—effectively a “pay-to-lose” mechanic if you had a flashy stamp. Now, they’re hidden unless you have direct line of sight.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Dev Team Perspectives on Balance Tweaks[/b][/h2]
Rather than repeat the changes:
[list][*][b]Penetration & Burst:[/b][list][*]The devs emphasized that too many high-penetration items at once create lethal “burst-heavy” scenarios. OB4 reduces some penetration values to see if it mitigates that “instant-delete” feel.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Healing & Anti-Heal:[/b][list][*]The community and top players alike voiced concerns about the power of healing comps. Developers are carefully buffing anti-heal durations so players can maintain pressure longer without removing healing from the game entirely.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Warrior/Guardian Tuning:[/b][list][*]Addressing underused items like Warrior’s Axe aligns with the devs’ broader goal: give different roles more item paths. The team wants players to discover a variety of valid build routes, not just “cookie cutter” ones.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2] [b]Community-Driven Questions & Future Plans[/b][/h2]
Here are a few behind-the-scenes bits [u]not[/u] spelled out in patch notes:
[list][*][b]Why Are Some Features Not in Yet?[/b][list][*][b]God Builders, Bracket Targeting, and HUD Customization[/b] require major engineering and UI time. The devs confirm these are in active development but come after core systems are stabilized.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]FPS Caps & Optimization[/b][list][*]120 FPS on all platforms remains a desired milestone; the devs need further optimization to ensure stable performance. They’re also looking at adding more in-between caps (e. g., 144 or custom caps) for different monitors.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Stylistic Approach[/b][list][*]The team is aiming for a “painterly” or “stylized” look that feels uniquely SMITE—rather than ultra-realism. Early on, feedback suggested the game was veering too realistic. Hence, the color palette and lighting are intentionally more vibrant and stylized.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Releasing Some Aspects Later[/b][list][*]You’ll notice not all newly ported gods launch with an Aspect. This is to let the community fully explore the base kit first. Artemis is a special case this patch, but expect more “post-release Aspects” going forward.[/*][/list][/*][*][b]Social/Party System Work[/b][list][*]Known invite/party formation bugs remain a major target. A dedicated sub-team is tackling these issues, and we’ll see incremental fixes rolling out in upcoming patches.[/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Feedback: The Engine That Drives Iteration[/b][/h2][list][*]The devs reiterated how crucial community insight is for refining game flow:[list][*][b]Tournament POVs & Creator Feedback[/b]: Big influences on tuning gods, from minor kit adjustments to broader item reworks.[/*][*][b]Ambassador Conversations[/b]: The internal community panels often bubble up issues (e. g., certain starts or items underperforming).[/*][/list][/*][*]Expect more [b]incremental changes[/b] to gold bounties, new item additions, and further assault/conquest tweaks based on real-world data.[/*][/list][h2] [b]Looking Ahead[/b][/h2][list][*][b]OB4[/b] hits very soon, with Artemis and her Aspect, plus many behind-the-scenes improvements.[/*][*][b]Awilix[/b] arrives next week—on track for March 3, unless scheduling shifts.[/*][*]Future dev talk topics: new Aspects (Baron Samedi is on deck), ongoing UI improvements, quality-of-life expansions (music packs, more party fixes), and continued game-mode polish.[/*][/list][h3][b]Stay Connected[/b][/h3][list][*]For [b]exact[/b] downtime or hotfix times, always check official [b]SMITE 2[/b] socials.[/*][*]If you haven’t already, dive into the [url=https://www.smite2.com/news/open-beta-4-update-notes/]OB4 Patch Notes[/url] for every detail on item/god changes.[/*][*]Keep the [b]feedback[/b] coming—through Titan Talk, official forums, and community channels. Your voice shapes the battleground.[/*][/list]
Thanks for reading, and we’ll see you Monday in [b]OB4[/b]!

notes.title: Titan Talks and Hotfix Roundup February 20th
notes.content:
The latest edition of Titan Talk was hosted by Isiah Kilgoon, bringing Smite fans the latest updates, bug fixes, and a community-driven discussion. This episode focused on addressing player questions and providing insight into the game's ongoing improvements and upcoming changes. Catch the entire episode:

[previewyoutube=tslKVetjJhY;full][/previewyoutube]


[h2]Recent Fixes, Balance Changes, and Community Feedback[/h2]

[h3]Balance Changes and Feedback Integration[/h3]
[list]
[*] Amaterasu and Hun Batz received balance tweaks to maintain fair and competitive gameplay.
[*] Community feedback is being considered for issues such as controller vibration intensity and other gameplay elements.
[/list]

[h2]Community Questions, Patch Notes, and Future Updates[/h2]
[h3]Classic Skin Tokens & Design Challenges[/h3]
[list]
[*] Clarifications were provided on Classic Skin Tokens, including acquisition methods and usage limitations. The crew is aware and working on better clarity for Skins labled as Classic that can’t be purchased with Tokens (Divine Legacy Skins and Darkheart Zeus)
[*] The team discussed the complexities of balancing gameplay features while incorporating community feedback. This is an ongoing and iterative process that we can’t do without everyone!
[/list]
[h3]Patch Notes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Acknowledgment of the need to improve documentation quality for patch notes compared to Smite 
[*]Radar has joined the team to revamp the patch notes process, ensuring clearer communication.
[/list]
[h3]Game Modes and Matchmaking[/h3]
[list]
[*] The current priority is refining existing modes like Conquest and Assault rather than introducing new ones.
[*] Ongoing discussions about ways to improve matchmaking and ranked gameplay for better competitive balance.
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay Issues, Console Fixes, and Visual Updates[/h2]
[h3]Thor’s Ultimate Indicator & Magi’s Balance[/h3]
[list]
[*] The team is investigating inconsistencies in Thor’s ultimate ability indicator, particularly linked to graphical settings.
[*] Players are encouraged to participate in testing Magi’s power levels to refine balance.

[/list]
[h3]Console Store and Performance Optimization[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixes targeting console store issues are set to be included in upcoming updates.
[*] Developers are working on addressing performance issues and lag in the profile tab across all platforms.
[/list]
[h3]Visual Updates & Godbuilder Progress[/h3]
[list]
[*] The team aims to balance familiar god designs with visual improvements that align with community expectations.
[*] Work continues on the Godbuilder system, with planned UI enhancements to streamline item build creation.
[/list]

[h2]Miscellaneous Updates and Final Q&A[/h2]

[h3]Chest Store and Controller Sensitivity[/h3]
[list]
[*] OB4 will Introduce new chests featuring classic skins and cross-generation content.
[*] The team remains open to controller settings adjustments based on player feedback.
[/list]

[h2]Game Pacing, Map Farm & Continued Engagement[/h2]
[list]
[*] Evaluating possible adjustments to game pacing and farm opportunities to maintain an engaging experience.
[*] They reaffirmed their commitment to active dialogue with players, including feedback collection through flash tests and regular updates.
[*] The team remains dedicated to ongoing development and refinements, ensuring the game evolves based on community input and in-game data analysis.
[/list]

Stay tuned for future episodes of Titan Talk as the team continues to bring exciting updates and engage with the Smite community!

notes.title: Achilles Enters the Battlegrounds of SMITE 2
notes.content:
The legends tell of Achilles, the greatest warrior of the Greeks, whose very name echoes with the glory of battle. He led a thousand ships to Troy, struck down the mighty Hector, and fell only to the treacherous arrow of Paris. But now, in SMITE 2, Achilles has returned—his fury unbound, his legend reborn, and his thirst for battle stronger than ever. The gods have called him back, but Achilles does not kneel—he fights for vengeance.

[b]Reimagined for SMITE 2 – A Deadlier Achilles[/b]

Achilles was a formidable warrior in SMITE, boasting a unique blend of adaptability and lethality. In SMITE 2, his combat prowess has been honed to perfection, bringing deeper decision-making and raw power to the battlefield. While his signature ability to don or remove his armor remains, new mechanics enhance his aggressive playstyle, rewarding those who wield him with precision.

[i]Passive: Gift of the Gods[/i]

Achilles' defining trait returns: the ability to choose between wearing armor or fighting unburdened. This choice shapes how he battles—armor grants bonus Health and Protections, while forsaking it increases his Strength and Movement Speed. In SMITE 2, this choice feels more meaningful than ever, allowing players to tailor Achilles to their preferred style.

[i]Shield of Achilles[/i]

A devastating punch with his shield that damages and stuns enemies in a short cone. Precision is key—strike the right target, and you can disrupt entire engagements, turning the tide of battle.

[i]Radiant Glory[/i]

Achilles channels the divine blessing of the gods, granting himself increased Strength, Protections, and Crowd Control Reduction. But in SMITE 2, this ability now offers more than just resilience—each ability hit during its duration heals Achilles, keeping him in the fight longer.

[i]Combat Dodge[/i]

The battlefield is Achilles' domain, and he moves through it with deadly efficiency. With Combat Dodge, he quickly evades and retaliates, striking enemies for significant Physical Damage. The ability rewards aggressive positioning and quick reflexes, making Achilles a nightmare for his foes.

[i]Ultimate Ability: Fatal Strike[/i]

Prepare for one of the most lethal executions in SMITE 2. Achilles dashes forward, striking down enemies and executing those at low health. Killing a god refreshes the ability, allowing him to chain executions up to five times. With sharper animations and a more visceral impact, Fatal Strike delivers true terror to the battleground.

[b]Aspect of Prowess – A New Way to Play[/b]

A warrior is never static, and Achilles now has a new way to define his legend. By choosing the Aspect of Prowess, his Combat Dodge gains a recast when striking Jungle Monsters or Bosses, making him a formidable presence in the jungle. Additionally, if he forgoes armor, his Spear Strike (basic attack) scales even harder, further rewarding risk-taking aggression. However, the cost is steep—Radiant Glory no longer grants protections or crowd control reduction, leaving Achilles more vulnerable to retaliation.

[b]The Return of a Legend[/b]

With refined combat mechanics, an emphasis on strategic play, and the triumphant return of his iconic execution, Achilles in SMITE 2 stands as an electrifying warrior with his name etched into history!
Take up your spear. Choose your path. And let the battlegrounds tremble before the wrath of Achilles.

[*] Fixed VGS popping on Release instead of on Trigger for gamepad
[/list]

Ranked matchmaking imposes a hard limit on the SR range in a match that expands over time. The longer a player waits, the wider the range possible.

Trio queue is healthy for the top end of the Ranked funnel, and brings in many new Ranked players, but under the standard set of Ranked matchmaking rules created undesirable outcomes, especially with top Ranked players.
Moving forward, we will treat Solo or Duo queueing as “Standard” Ranked queueing, and Trio queueing under its own set of rules.
Parties of size 3 will be evaluated based on the maximum SR of their party (as opposed to average SR with Duos)
Parties of size 3 will be hard limited to a range of 1,000 SR, capping at 5,000 SR
311v2111 was removed from the viable matchmaking pool in Ranked

notes.title: Introducing the Wandering Market!
notes.content:
[h1]Step right up, traveler, and discover the Wandering Market![/h1]

This ever-changing bazaar is your gateway to treasures untold in SMITE 2. Earn XP through daily gameplay and quests to progress along the reward track, collecting Coins as you go. Use your Coins to unlock rewards from a trove of Collections, with a new themed Collection arriving every 8 weeks. Best of all, participation is FREE for everyone—but upgrading to Premium unlocks even greater riches! The Market’s doors are always open for adventure. What treasures will you claim? The choice is yours!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44832142/38373c427354d4042a7083e0eeb8c42a91aa40cd.png[/img]

[h1]Collections and Rewards[/h1]

    [h3]What is included in each Collection?[/h3]

    Each Collection features four pages, with one unique Skin per page. Free players can only access the first page, while Premium players unlock additional pages by spending Coins progressively. Note that contents will vary in each Collection.

    [h3]What can free players earn?[/h3]

    Free players can earn all items on the first page of each Collection, including a variation of high-value rewards like Diamonds, Skins, and cosmetics. Premium players gain access to additional pages with more rewards.

    [h3]Can I preview the rewards before deciding to participate?[/h3]

    Yes, players can preview all rewards, free and premium, in each Collection before spending Coins or upgrading to Premium.

    [h3]Can I choose the rewards I unlock within a Collection?[/h3]

    Yes! Players can select rewards in any order within each page, offering complete control to buy what you like.

    [h3]Can I skip a Collection and come back to it later?[/h3]

    You can skip a Collection, earn Coins, and return to it later to unlock free rewards or upgrade that Collection to Premium at any time.

    [h3]Do I need to complete one Collection before starting another?[/h3]

    No, you don’t need to complete one Collection before starting another. You can progress any of the active Collections in the Wandering Market at your own pace.

[h1]Progression and XP[/h1]

    [h3]How do I earn XP and Coins to spend in the Wandering Market?[/h3]

    You earn XP by playing matches and completing daily quests. XP progresses you along the reward track, unlocking Coins at each level. Coins are then used to purchase items within each Collection.

    [h3]Do free players earn XP at the same rate as Premium players?[/h3]

    Yes! XP progression is identical for both free and Premium players.

    [h3]Do I need to play every day to keep up?[/h3]

    No! The system is designed to accommodate different playstyles, allowing players to progress at their own pace without daily pressure.

[h1]Coins and Spending[/h1]

    [h3]Can I spend Coins across different Collections?[/h3]

    Yes! Coins are universal and can be used in any Collection available – past, present, or future.

    [h3]What happens if I hit the Coin cap?[/h3]

    If you reach the Coin cap, you’ll stop earning additional Market XP, even if you complete the daily quests or play games. However, as soon as you spend Coins and drop below the cap, you’ll be able to start earning Market XP again. The first page of each Collection provides rewards for free players to spend their coins or you can upgrade to the Premium Pass to continue spending your Coins on more pages!

    [h3]Why is there a limit on how many Coins I can hold?[/h3]

    The Coin cap ensures balanced progression, prevents excessive hoarding, and maintains fairness among all levels of players.

[h1]Collection Availability[/h1]
 
    [h3]How long will a Collection be available?[/h3]

    Currently, there’s no set end date for Collections in the Wandering Market. We’ll periodically review this to address any potential UI challenges this might create. If changes are needed, we’ll ensure players receive clear communication and plenty of advance notice.

notes.title: SMITE 2 is now FREE TO PLAY!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=CTbb9B3UinQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Join the Battleground of the Gods: SMITE 2 is Now Free-to-Play![/h3]

Step into the all-new SMITE 2 Open Beta and experience the next evolution of third-person action MOBA combat—now powered by Unreal Engine 5. If you crave challenging competition, intense gameplay, ability-driven team fights, and godly mythological themes, it’s time to see why over 40 million players are hooked on SMITE. Become a God today!

[h3]What’s New in the SMITE 2 Open Beta?[/h3]

[list]
[*] 45 Gods — Including the brand-new God Aladdin (and his mighty Genie).
[*] 6 Game Modes — Featuring brand-new Joust, Duel, and Assault alongside an updated Conquest map with fresh objectives.
[*] 20 Aspects — Transform your favorite Gods with game-changing playstyle twists.
[*] Countless Improvements — Months of Closed Alpha feedback have shaped SMITE 2 into a more refined, optimized experience.
[/list]
